question: What is the main benefit of giving medication directly into a joint space?

options.A: Achieving high local drug concentration with minimal systemic side effects
options.B: Ensuring rapid absorption directly into the systemic arterial circulation
options.C: Preventing any possibility of local tissue damage at the injection site
options.D: Eliminating the need for strict sterile technique during administration

explanation: Injecting medication straight into the joint puts the medicine right where it is needed while keeping it from spreading through the rest of the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why is keeping the area completely sterile so important during a joint injection?

options.A: Bacteria introduced into the joint space can cause septic arthritis
options.B: Skin flora will neutralize the therapeutic effect of local anesthetics
options.C: Joint cavities are prone to severe infections due to limited vascular supply
options.D: Unsterile technique immediately deactivates the administered steroid

explanation: The inner joint space easily traps germs, which can multiply quickly and cause a dangerous joint infection known as septic arthritis. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which type of drug is commonly injected into joints to bring down swelling and inflammation?
explanation: Corticosteroids are strong anti-inflammatory medications that help calm swelling and ease pain right inside the joint. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h2)

question: Viscosupplementation agents like hyaluronic acid are mostly used to manage which condition?
explanation: These agents help restore fluid cushioning in joints that have worn down from osteoarthritis. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which situation is a major reason NOT to perform a joint injection?

options.C: Mild chronic pain during physical activity
options.D: Active infection in or near the target joint

explanation: Pushing a needle through infected skin or into an infected joint will push bacteria deeper and make the infection worse. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h3)

question: A patient scheduled for a knee joint injection takes warfarin. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Cancel the procedure without informing the doctor
options.B: Administer a dose of vitamin K immediately
options.C: Proceed with the injection and apply firm pressure later
options.D: Notify the physician to review the coagulation profile

explanation: Blood thinners raise the risk of bleeding inside the joint, so the care team must check clotting status first. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which skin cleanser is most commonly used to prep the skin before a joint injection?
explanation: Chlorhexidine quickly kills skin germs and keeps working to lower the risk of infection. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why must skin antiseptic agents dry completely before the nurse inserts the needle?

options.A: To prevent the skin from slipping during needle puncture
options.B: To ensure the adhesive bandage sticks properly afterward
options.C: To stop the patient from experiencing a burning sensation
options.D: To allow sufficient time for microbial destruction to occur

explanation: Antiseptics need a little time to work and dry fully to kill off germs effectively before the skin is pierced. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h4)

question: What self-care advice is usually given to a patient right after a joint injection?

options.B: Applying ice and resting the joint
options.C: Soaking the joint in a hot water bath

explanation: Rest and cold packs help keep swelling down and ease discomfort after the joint has been poked. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h5)

question: What normal reaction can happen a few hours after a patient receives a joint steroid injection?

options.A: Immediate systemic reduction in blood pressure
options.B: Permanent numbness in the surrounding muscles
options.C: Complete disappearance of all cartilage damage
options.D: Temporary flare of joint pain before relief begins

explanation: Some people experience a steroid flare, where the joint temporarily feels more sore as the body reacts to the medication crystals before the pain starts to fade. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which symptom helps a nurse tell the difference between a normal post-injection flare and septic arthritis?

options.A: Persistent fever and progressive worsening of joint pain
options.B: Slight redness around the puncture site without swelling
options.C: Temporary stiffness experienced the morning after injection
options.D: Mild soreness that resolves within twenty-four hours

explanation: Septic arthritis is an actual bacterial infection marked by fever and severe pain that gets worse, unlike simple soreness that goes away on its own. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h6)

question: A patient with diabetes notices high blood sugar readings at home after getting a joint steroid injection. What causes this?

options.A: Systemic absorption of the injected corticosteroid
options.B: Dietary indiscretion following the joint procedure
options.C: Inadequate skin preparation prior to the injection
options.D: Failure to take oral hypoglycemic drugs on time

explanation: Even though the shot is given locally in the joint, some of the steroid enters the bloodstream and can push blood sugar levels up in diabetic patients. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h6)
